result:
Основываясь на прочитанном коде Dog и общей информации о паттернах оркестрации, могу предоставить анализ с точки зрения prompt engineering:

```json
{
  "strengths_dog": [
    "Built-in prompt assembly system (assemble_prompt) with multi-layer composition: specialists + team tone + block prompt",
    "Template substitution via {{ filename.json }} placeholders with automatic JSON file loading from task outputs",
    "Structured prompt versioning through YAML workflow configs with explicit prompt field per stage",
    "Context management through task_input/task_dir variables passed to logic scripts via stdin JSON",
    "Three-phase logic system (pre/post/validate) allowing pre-processing, post-processing and validation of Claude outputs",
    "File-based data flow between stages - each block saves results to JSON with envelope format (stage, result, timestamp)",
    "Team tone injection - loads collaboration_tone from team YAML files and prepends to all prompts",
    "Specialist instructions loading - reads .md files from agents/specialists/ and includes in prompt assembly",
    "Support for both Anthropic and OpenRouter APIs with configurable models via environment variables",
    "Result envelope extraction - automatically unwraps nested JSON from Claude responses",
    "Variable substitution preserves whitespace in {{ file.json }} patterns for clean prompt formatting",
    "Task-scoped context - all blocks in workflow share task_id and can access shared outputs directory",
    "Schema validation engine integration (Phase 1) - validates workflow structure before execution"
  ],
  "strengths_conductor": [
    "Lightweight shell-based orchestration - minimal dependencies, pure bash execution",
    "Simple text-based prompt management - likely uses heredocs or template files",
    "Direct process control without Python overhead",
    "Unix philosophy - compose simple tools via pipes and redirects",
    "Easy to debug with standard shell tools (set -x, logging)",
    "Fast startup time - no interpreter initialization",
    "Environment variable substitution built into shell",
    "Can leverage full Unix toolchain (jq, sed, awk) for prompt transformation"
  ],
  "weaknesses_dog": [
    "No built-in prompt versioning/history tracking - relies on git for workflow YAML changes",
    "Limited template language - only supports {{ file.json }} substitution, no conditionals or loops",
    "Prompt assembly is opaque - assembled prompt only logged to dog.log, not easily inspectable during development",
    "No prompt optimization features - no token counting, cost estimation, or prompt compression",
    "Hard-coded envelope format - result wrapping in {stage, result, timestamp} is not configurable",
    "Context window management not addressed - no automatic truncation or summarization",
    "No A/B testing support for prompt variants",
    "Specialist and team tone concatenation is naive - just joins with newlines and separators",
    "No support for structured outputs or function calling - treats all Claude responses as text",
    "Variable substitution only works for JSON files - cannot substitute plain text or environment variables in prompts",
    "Logic scripts receive context via stdin JSON but format is implicit - no schema enforcement",
    "No built-in retry or fallback strategies for API failures",
    "Prompt templates are embedded in workflow YAML - changes require editing workflow files directly"
  ],
  "weaknesses_conductor": [
    "No structured prompt composition - likely manual string concatenation in shell scripts",
    "Limited JSON handling - must use external tools like jq for parsing",
    "No type safety - everything is text, easy to have substitution errors",
    "Difficult to maintain complex multi-stage prompts across multiple shell scripts",
    "No built-in API client - must use curl with manual header management",
    "Shell quoting and escaping complexity when dealing with multi-line prompts",
    "No structured logging of prompts and responses - relies on manual echo statements",
    "Hard to implement sophisticated data flow patterns - limited to files and environment variables",
    "No built-in validation or schema checking for prompt templates",
    "Context management is manual - no automatic passing of previous stage outputs",
    "Versioning requires external tooling - no built-in prompt history",
    "Limited error handling - shell error handling is basic compared to Python try/catch"
  ],
  "recommendation": "From a prompt engineering perspective, Dog is significantly more sophisticated than Conductor. Dog provides:\n\n1. STRUCTURED PROMPT COMPOSITION: The three-layer assembly (team tone + specialists + block prompt) allows clean separation of concerns - collaboration style, domain expertise, and task-specific instructions. This is superior to manual concatenation.\n\n2. DATA FLOW ARCHITECTURE: The {{ filename.json }} substitution with automatic envelope unwrapping creates a clean pipeline where each stage's Claude output becomes the next stage's input. This enables complex multi-turn prompt chains.\n\n3. LOGIC PHASES: The pre/post/validate hooks allow prompt engineering workflows like: (a) pre-phase: fetch data and build dynamic context, (b) Claude phase: main reasoning, (c) post-phase: extract structured data from response, (d) validate-phase: check output quality.\n\n4. TASK-SCOPED CONTEXT: The task_dir/task_input system provides persistent context across workflow execution, enabling stateful prompt engineering patterns.\n\nHowever, Dog has significant gaps for advanced prompt engineering:\n\n- NO PROMPT OPTIMIZATION: Missing token counting, cost estimation, prompt compression\n- NO EXPERIMENTATION SUPPORT: No A/B testing, prompt variants, or performance tracking\n- LIMITED TEMPLATE LANGUAGE: Only simple variable substitution, no conditionals/loops\n- OPAQUE EXECUTION: Assembled prompts only in logs, hard to inspect during development\n\nRECOMMENDATION: Use Dog as the base orchestrator but add:\n1. Prompt inspection mode (--dry-run flag to print assembled prompts without calling API)\n2. Token counting integration (use tiktoken or similar before API calls)\n3. Prompt template inheritance (allow blocks to extend/override base prompts)\n4. Structured output support (add JSON schema validation for Claude responses)\n5. Prompt versioning metadata (track which prompt version produced which result)\n6. Context window management (automatic truncation strategies when context exceeds limits)\n\nFor simple linear workflows, Conductor's shell-based approach is adequate. But for complex prompt engineering with multi-agent collaboration, dynamic context, and quality validation, Dog's architecture is superior - it just needs more prompt-specific features added to its existing foundation."
}
```
